pages.description: How inboxes are created, receive mail, expire, and are deleted.
pages.text:
An inbox moves through three states.CreatedCreated
Create inbox returns an address immediately. The inbox starts with an empty message list and a ttl in seconds (default 3600, maximum 86400).ActiveActive
While active, the inbox accepts every message sent to its address. Messages are parsed on arrival; see Get message for the parsed shape, including the content variants.ExpiredExpired
When the ttl elapses the inbox stops receiving mail but stays readable for 24 hours, so a slow CI job can still inspect what arrived. After that it is deleted, together with its messages and attachments.Expiry is measured from creation, not from the last message. Extend the ttl with Update inbox if a test needs more time.TagsTags
Tags are free-form labels (at most 10 per inbox) used by List inboxes filters and by webhook filters. Choose stable tags such as signup-flow rather than per-run identifiers.

  timeout: 30_000,
});

pages.description: Receive your first test email in under five minutes. You need an API key from the dashboard and a project that sends email.
pages.text:
Before you start
Create an API key in the dashboard and export it as TESTINBOX_API_KEY. Sandbox and production keys are separate; see Authentication.Create an inbox
Every test gets its own address. A short ttl keeps the sandbox clean; the inbox is deleted when it expires.const inbox = await client.inboxes.create({ ttl: 600 });
Returns an Inbox with address and expiresAt.Trigger your application
Use the inbox address wherever your application would send email: a sign-up form, a password reset, an invoice.await app.signUp({ email: inbox.address });
Wait for an email
wait() blocks until a message matching your criteria arrives or the timeout passes. Match by subject, sender, or body.const message = await inbox.messages.wait({ subject: /verify/i, timeout: 30_000 });
Assert its contents
expect(message.links[0]).toContain("/verify?token=");
Choose your clientChoose your client
TypeScript
import { TestInbox } from "@testinbox/client";

const client = new TestInbox({ apiKey: process.env.TESTINBOX_API_KEY });
Python
from testinbox import TestInbox

client = TestInbox(api_key=os.environ["TESTINBOX_API_KEY"])
cURL
curl -X POST https://api.testinbox.email/v1/inboxes \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $TESTINBOX_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"ttl": 600}'
